docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
PyCSP v1.5.0

Software documentation

PyCSP is a collection of libraries for the analysis, model reduction and ODE integration of reacting systems using the computational singular perturbation (CSP) method and its extensions, including the Tangential Stretching Rate (TSR).

It provides tools for the local characterization of the chemical dynamics, built on the eigen-decomposition of the Jacobian of the chemical source term:

  • the CSP kernel: eigenvalues, right/left basis vectors, mode amplitudes and timescales;
  • exhausted (fast) modes, and the fast/active/slow subspace partitioning;
  • the Tangential Stretching Rate, and its extension to reaction-diffusion-convection systems;
  • amplitude and timescale participation indices, fast/slow importance indices, CSP pointers and species classification;
  • skeletal mechanism generation (CSP simplification);
  • two CSP-based ODE integrators (CSP solver and G-Scheme).

The theory behind these tools is summarized in three pages: CSP and TSR analysis, mechanism simplification and CSP solver and G-Scheme.

docs.title: Changes with respect to previous version (v1.4)
docs.text:
Bug fixes that change numerical results:

  • Constant-pressure Jacobian. The species columns were evaluated at constant density instead of constant pressure: perturbing a mass fraction changed the pressure. All Jacobians are now taken holding the thermodynamic constraint of the problem fixed (pressure for const_p, density for const_v). This affects every constant-pressure CSP/TSR quantity. In the H\(_2\)/air ignition test case, the Jacobian changes by up to about 1% (relative to its largest entries) and the TSR by up to 5% near ignition, while the number of exhausted modes is unchanged.
  • Per-reaction Jacobian contributions (jac_contribution). The same constant-pressure correction; for constant-volume problems the temperature column is now taken at constant density. The contributions now sum to the Jacobian in both formulations, which affects the timescale participation indices (TPI) and TSR-TPI.
  • Timescale participation indices of complex-conjugate modes. The indices of a complex pair summed to zero; they now decompose \(\mathrm{Re}(\lambda)\).
  • Constrained Jacobian (jacobiantype='constrained') for constant-volume problems. It now uses the internal energies and \(c_v\) (constant internal-energy constraint) instead of enthalpies and \(c_p\).
  • TSR. Modes with zero eigenvalue are now excluded consistently with the exhausted-modes calculation.
  • utils.integrate_batch_constV now sets constRho to the density of the actual mixture.

Other bug fixes:

  • calc_subspaces (and findH) no longer crash with the kinetic and constrained Jacobian types.
  • The thermochemical state of the object is now always restored after Jacobian evaluations (it was left perturbed with the kinetic/constrained types).
  • jacobian_diagonal for constant-volume problems used the constant-pressure source term.
  • TPI are not available for jacobiantype='constrained' (the thermal correction is not split by reaction): a NotImplementedError is raised instead of returning inconsistent values.
  • utils.save_CSP_plots: fixed crashes with short time series, and the rate-of-progress and RHS plots.
  • CSPsimplify.get_tsrtarget no longer fails for TSRtol = 1.
  • The order of the two eigenvalues of a complex-conjugate pair (negative imaginary part first) no longer depends on the platform's sorting algorithm.
  • CSPsolver/GScheme.set_integrator raise a ValueError on unknown keywords instead of exiting the interpreter; profiling() no longer divides by zero.

New features and changes:

  • Optional norm_cut argument for the CSP indices (calc_CSPindices, calc_TSRindices, CSPsimplify.norm_cut): rows whose sum of absolute contributions is below the cut are set to zero instead of being normalized. Contributed by students.
  • utils.shared_reactor, for creating Cantera reactors that share the CanteraCSP object across Cantera versions.
  • A pytest test-suite with correctness tests and golden-master regression tests, run by continuous integration.
  • Removed soln2cti.py and soln2ck.py, which only worked with Cantera 2.x. Use Cantera's Solution.write_yaml() and Solution.write_chemkin() instead.
  • Removed unused legacy functions (findM_original, setEwt_original, modeContribution_original, CSPtiming).
  • Documentation moved from PDF to this website.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
PyCSP relies on Cantera ≥ 3.0.0, numpy and matplotlib. Pandas is required as well for minor functions such as profiling. PyCSP v1.5.0 works with the latest Cantera release (3.2.0): the full test-suite passes with Cantera 3.2.0 (Python 3.12, numpy 2) as well as with the oldest supported version, Cantera 3.0 (Python 3.10, numpy 1.23). The continuous-integration workflow tests Cantera 3.0, 3.1 and the latest release on every change. The Python version must comply with Cantera.

For older versions of Cantera (2.5), download release v1.2.1.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
PyCSP is available on PyPI as PyCSP-lib:

$ pip install PyCSP-lib

Installation using Anaconda is recommended. In such case, proceed as follows via command line:

$ git clone https://github.com/rmalpica/PyCSP.git
$ cd $PATH_TO_PyCSP_MAIN_FOLDER
$ conda create --name pycsp --channel conda-forge python=3.12 cantera numpy matplotlib pandas
$ conda activate pycsp
$ pip install $PATH_TO_PyCSP_MAIN_FOLDER

Alternatively, once the prerequisite libraries are installed, the installation may be performed via command line as follows:

$ git clone https://github.com/rmalpica/PyCSP.git
$ pip install $PATH_TO_PyCSP_MAIN_FOLDER

Use pip install -e $PATH_TO_PyCSP_MAIN_FOLDER for an editable (development) installation.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The test-suite uses pytest. To test the installation, proceed as follows via command line:

$ cd $PATH_TO_PyCSP_MAIN_FOLDER
$ pip install pytest
$ pytest

The suite contains:

File Content test_rhs.py, test_rhs_constV.py The chemical source term equals \(\mathcal{S}\,\mathbf{r}\) and the Cantera net production rates, at constant pressure and constant volume. test_kernel.py Properties of the CSP kernel along an H\(_2\)/air ignition: bi-orthonormality, ordering, conserved modes, \(\mathbf{g} = \mathbf{A}\,\mathbf{f}\). test_correctness.py Jacobians against independent references (constraint, chain rule, elemental conservation, constrained manifold), sum of per-reaction contributions, TPI decomposition of the eigenvalues, state restoration. test_norm_cut.py The optional norm_cut of the CSP indices. test_utils_and_solvers.py Utilities, simplifier and CSP integrators. test_golden.py Golden-master regression: kernel, M, H, TSR, projectors and indices at stored states, CSP solver, G-Scheme and simplifier runs.

The test files test_kernel.py, test_rhs.py and test_rhs_constV.py can also be run as scripts from the tests folder, to plot their results:

$ cd tests
$ python test_kernel.py

test_kernel.py plots the evolution of the system's eigenvalues during the ignition of a constant-pressure reactor.

Figure 1: Typical results: time evolution of temperature, OH, H and H2 in a constant-pressure reactor (left) and of the system's eigenvalues (right).

Golden masters

The reference data of test_golden.py are stored in tests/golden/golden_h2.npz. They are regenerated only on purpose, after a deliberate and reviewed change of results, with python tests/golden/make_golden.py.

docs.title: jac_contribution()
docs.text: Computes contributions of each reaction to numerical Jacobian. Given that g = Sr = Sum_k S_k r^k, it follows that J(g) = Sum_k^(2nr) J_k, where J_k = Jac(S_k r^k) S_k r^k is the product of the k-th column of the matrix S and the k-th component of the vector r. Returns a (2*Nr, nv, nv) array [jacK], whose sum over the first axis equals the (full or kinetic) Jacobian.

docs.title: jacobian_diagonal_const_p()
docs.text: Computes (an approx. to) the diagonal of the numerical Jacobian at constant pressure. Returns a N_s+1 array [diagjac].

docs.title: jacobian_diagonal_const_v()
docs.text: Computes (an approx. to) the diagonal of the numerical Jacobian at constant density. Returns a N_s+1 array [diagjac].

docs.title: jacThermal()
docs.text: Correction that constrains the species Jacobian to the manifold of constant enthalpy (const_p) or constant internal energy (const_v): J_constrained = J_YY - jacThermal, with jacThermal[i,j] = dg_i/dT * e_j/c, where e_j = h_j, c = cp (const_p) or e_j = u_j, c = cv (const_v), mass-specific species properties.

docs.text: Computes subspaces partitioning (M and H). Optional arguments are rtol and atol for the calculation of M, and rtol and atol for the calculation of H. If not provided, uses default or previously set values

docs.title: calc_TSR(**kwargs)
docs.text: Computes number of exhausted modes (M) and the TSR. Optional arguments are rtol and atol for the calculation of M. If not provided, uses default or previously set values. The calculated value of M can be retrieved by passing the optional argument getM=True

docs.title: calc_TSRindices(**kwargs)
docs.text: Computes number of exhausted modes (M), the TSR and its indices. Optional argument is type, which can be timescale or amplitude. Default value is amplitude. Other optional arguments are rtol and atol for the calculation of M. If not provided, uses default or previously set values. The TSR value can be retrieved by passing getTSR=True, in which case the method returns (TSR, indices). Optional norm_cut (scalar or nv-long array, default None): with index_norm='abs', modes whose CSP indices have a sum of absolute contributions smaller than norm_cut get zero indices (units of that sum: 1/s for type='timescale', the mode-amplitude units for type='amplitude').

docs.title: calc_CSPindices(**kwargs)
docs.text: Computes number of exhausted modes (M) and the CSP Indices. Boolean keywords select the indices to compute (all default False): API (amplitude participation), TPI (timescale participation), Impo (fast/slow importance), species_type (fast/slow/trace species). Returns [API, TPI, Ifast, Islow, species_type] (None for those not requested), plus M if getM=True. Optional arguments are rtol and atol for the calculation of M. If not provided, uses default or previously set values. Optional norm_cut (scalar or nv-long array, default None): with index_norm='abs', rows (modes for API/TPI, variables for Ifast/Islow) whose sum of absolute contributions is smaller than norm_cut are set to zero instead of being normalized (units of that sum: the rate of the mode amplitude or variable, 1/s for TPI).

docs.title: calc_extended_TSR(**kwargs)
docs.text: Computes number of Extended exhausted modes (Mext) and the extended TSR. Caller must provide either a diffusion rhs with the keyword diff or a convection rhs with the keyword conv, or both (nv-long arrays). Optional arguments are rtol and atol for the calculation of Mext. If not provided, uses default or previously set values. The calculated value of Mext can be retrieved by passing the optional argument getMext=True

docs.title: calc_extended_TSRindices(**kwargs)
docs.text: Computes number of Extended exhausted modes (Mext), the extended TSR and its indices. Caller must provide either a diffusion rhs with the keyword diff or a convection rhs with the keyword conv, or both (nv-long arrays). Other optional arguments are rtol and atol for the calculation of Mext. If not provided, uses default or previously set values. The extended TSR can be retrieved by passing the optional argument getTSRext=True, in which case the method returns (TSR_ext, indices). Indices refer to the 2Nr reactions, then the nv convection and the nv diffusion terms.

docs.title: detectFrozenModes(M, stateYT, Revec, Levec, Smat, rvec, rtol, atol)
docs.text:
Identifies frozen modes among the M exhausted modes (or all modes, if needed). A mode is frozen if the sum of absolute projected reaction rates is small.

Parameters:

M : int Number of exhausted modes (returned by findM). stateYT : array State vector [Species... , T]. Revec : array Right eigenvectors (rows). Levec : array Left eigenvectors (rows). Smat : array Stoichiometric matrix. rvec : array Reaction rates vector. rtol : float Relative tolerance. atol : float Absolute tolerance.

Returns:

frozen_indices : list Indices of modes that are frozen.

docs.title: Classes, attributes and methods
docs.text:
PyCSP is organized in the following modules:

Module Content ThermoKinetics.py class CanteraThermoKinetics: source term, generalized stoichiometric matrix, rates of progress and Jacobians of homogeneous reactors at constant pressure or constant volume. Functions.py class CanteraCSP: CSP kernel, exhausted modes, subspaces, TSR, CSP and TSR indices. Solver.py class CSPsolver: CSP-based ODE integrator. GScheme.py class GScheme: G-Scheme ODE integrator. Simplify.py class CSPsimplify: skeletal mechanism generation. utils.py reactors, data storage and plotting utilities.

The class hierarchy is cantera.Solution → CanteraThermoKinetics → CanteraCSP, so that a CanteraCSP object is also a Cantera Solution, and all of Cantera's attributes and methods are available.

An automatically generated listing of the docstrings is available in the API reference.

docs.title: class CanteraCSP
docs.text:
This class inherits attributes and methods from the CanteraThermoKinetics class, which is in turn a derived class of Cantera's Solution class (multilevel inheritance), and extends their capabilities by adding computational singular perturbation (CSP)-related class methods. Hence, the constructor for this class is equivalent to the constructor of Cantera's Solution class. The proper way to instantiate CanteraCSP objects is by using species and reactions defined in an input file, e.g. hydrogen.yaml:

import PyCSP.Functions as csp
gas = csp.CanteraCSP('hydrogen.yaml')

The definitions of all the CSP quantities are given in the Theory page.

Kernel caching

The CSP kernel is recomputed lazily: the calc_* methods and get_kernel() recompute it only if an attribute of the object has been set since the last calculation (e.g. TPY, Y, constP, set_stateYT(...)). State changes made internally by Cantera, e.g. by a ReactorNet advancing a reactor that shares the object, are not detected. In that case, set the state explicitly (e.g. gas.TPY = gas.TPY) or call update_kernel() before querying the kernel.

docs.title: Instance attributes
docs.text: jacobiantype Type (string). Set/get the Jacobian type. Available choices are: 'full', 'kinetic', 'constrained' (see Theory). Defaults to 'full'. Note that this choice affects the dimension of the system (\(N_v = N_s+1\) for full, \(N_v = N_s\) otherwise), and in turn the dimension of the CSP-related attributes (eigenvalues, eigenvectors, timescales, amplitudes). rtol Type (float). Set/get the CSP relative tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation. Defaults to 1.0e-2. atol Type (float). Set/get the CSP absolute tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation. Defaults to 1.0e-8. rhs Type ([N\(_v\)] array of float, read-only). Get the chemical source term used for the CSP calculations. jac Type ([N\(_v\) \(\times\) N\(_v\)] array of float, read-only). Get the Jacobian of the chemical source term used for the CSP calculations. evals Type ([N\(_v\)] array of complex, read-only). Get the Jacobian eigenvalues, sorted by decreasing modulus. The last \(N_{el}\) (number of elements) eigenvalues are set to zero. Revec Type ([N\(_v\) \(\times\) N\(_v\)] array of float, read-only). Get the matrix of the Jacobian right eigenvectors (CSP basis vectors \(\mathbf{a}_i\)). The eigenvectors are assembled as row vectors, hence the i-th eigenvector can be accessed using Revec[i]. Note that the properly defined right eigenvectors matrix is the transpose of Revec. Complex-conjugate pairs are stored as real and imaginary parts. Levec Type ([N\(_v\) \(\times\) N\(_v\)] array of float, read-only). Get the matrix of the Jacobian left eigenvectors (CSP co-basis vectors \(\mathbf{b}^i\)), obtained by inversion of the right eigenvectors matrix. The eigenvectors are assembled as row vectors, hence the i-th eigenvector can be accessed using Levec[i]. f Type ([N\(_v\)] array of positive float, read-only). Get the CSP mode amplitudes. tau Type ([N\(_v\)] array of float, read-only). Get the modes timescales \(\tau_i = 1/|\lambda_i|\) (\(10^{20}\) for zero eigenvalues). index_norm Type (string). Available choices are: 'abs', 'none'. Defaults to 'abs'. Set the way Importance and Participation indices are normalized. When 'abs', indices are normalized with their 1-norm (sum of absolute values). This means that their absolute values sum to 1. When 'none', indices are not normalized (to be used for integral indices only). classify_traces Type (boolean). When True (default), the species classification also identifies trace species. nUpdates Type (int, read-only). Get the number of kernel updates, starting from the instantiation of the object.

docs.title: Class methods
docs.text:
update_kernel() Updates the CSP kernel (evals, Revec, Levec, f, tau), based on the current thermochemical state, employing the Jacobian formulation specified by setting either constP or constRho, and the Jacobian type specified with jacobiantype. Does not return any output. get_kernel() Returns the content of the [evals, Revec, Levec, f] attributes. If any attributes of the instance are changed with respect to the previous kernel calculation, the kernel is recomputed and returned. calc_exhausted_modes()

Computes and returns the number of exhausted modes \(M\) (int).

Optional keyword arguments:

  • rtol = float. Relative tolerance. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
  • atol = float. Absolute tolerance. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
calc_subspaces()

Computes and returns the indices \(M\) and \(H\) (also known as Tail and Head in the G-Scheme nomenclature [6]) corresponding to the subspaces partitioning into fast/active/slow modes [0:M], [M:H], [H:N] (int, int).

Optional keyword arguments:

  • rtolTail = float. Relative tolerance for M. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
  • atolTail = float. Absolute tolerance for M. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
  • rtolHead = float. Relative tolerance for H. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
  • atolHead = float. Absolute tolerance for H. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
calc_TSR()

Computes the number of exhausted modes and the Tangential Stretching Rate. Returns the Tangential Stretching Rate (float), or [TSR, M] if getM=True.

Optional keyword arguments:

  • rtol = float. Relative tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
  • atol = float. Absolute tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
  • getM = boolean. If True, the number of exhausted modes is returned as well.
calc_CSPindices()

Computes the number of exhausted modes and returns the requested CSP indices: amplitude participation indices (API), timescale participation indices (TPI), fast and slow importance indices, and the species classification (fast/slow/trace), as the list [API, TPI, Ifast, Islow, species_type] ([N\(_v \times\) 2N\(_r\)] array of float for each index, [N\(_v\)] array of strings for the classification). The quantities that are not requested are returned as None. If getM=True, \(M\) is appended to the list.

Optional keyword arguments:

  • API = boolean. If True, computes the amplitude participation indices. Defaults to False.
  • TPI = boolean. If True, computes the timescale participation indices. Defaults to False. Not available for jacobiantype='constrained'.
  • Impo = boolean. If True, computes the fast and slow importance indices. Defaults to False.
  • species_type = boolean. If True, computes the species classification. Defaults to False.
  • rtol = float. Relative tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation.
  • atol = float. Absolute tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation.
  • getM = boolean. If True, the number of exhausted modes is returned as well.
  • norm_cut = float or [N\(_v\)] array of float. With index_norm='abs', the rows whose sum of absolute contributions is smaller than norm_cut (a scalar, or one value per row) are set to zero instead of being normalized. The rows are modes for API and TPI, and variables for the importance indices. The units are those of the contributions: the rate of the mode amplitude or of the variable, and 1/s for the TPI. Defaults to None (no cut). New in v1.5.
calc_TSRindices()

Computes and returns the Tangential Stretching Rate amplitude (TSR-API) or timescale participation indices (TSR-TPI) ([2N\(_r\)] array of float). If getTSR=True, returns the tuple (TSR, indices).

Optional keyword arguments:

  • type = string. If 'amplitude', the TSR-API are returned. If 'timescale', the TSR-TPI are returned. Defaults to 'amplitude'. The 'timescale' type is not available for jacobiantype='constrained'.
  • rtol = float. Relative tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation.
  • atol = float. Absolute tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation.
  • getTSR = boolean. If True, the TSR is returned as well.
  • norm_cut = float or [N\(_v\)] array of float. Cut on the per-mode API or TPI (see calc_CSPindices). New in v1.5.
calc_extended_TSR()

Computes the number of extended exhausted modes (\(M_{ext}\)) and the extended Tangential Stretching Rate, for systems with transport. Returns the extended TSR (float), or [TSR_ext, Mext] if getMext=True.

Optional keyword arguments (at least one of diff and conv should be given):

  • diff = [N\(_v\)] array of float. Diffusion right hand side. Array containing the diffusion term of the mass fractions of all the species and of the temperature: \([\,D_1, \dots, D_{N_s}, D_T\,]\). The unit of measure must be [1/s] and [K/s]. The order of the \(D_i\) values must comply with the species ordering set at the class instantiation.
  • conv = [N\(_v\)] array of float. Convection right hand side \([\,C_1, \dots, C_{N_s}, C_T\,]\), with the same units and ordering.
  • rtol = float. Relative tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
  • atol = float. Absolute tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation. If not specified, the instance attribute is employed.
  • getMext = boolean. If True, the extended number of exhausted modes is returned as well.
calc_extended_TSRindices()

Computes and returns the amplitude participation indices to the extended Tangential Stretching Rate ([2N\(_r\)+N\(_v\)+N\(_v\)] array of float): the 2N\(_r\) reactions followed by the N\(_v\) convection and the N\(_v\) diffusion terms. If getTSRext=True, returns the tuple (TSR_ext, indices).

Optional keyword arguments:

  • diff =, conv = as in calc_extended_TSR.
  • rtol = float. Relative tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation.
  • atol = float. Absolute tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation.
  • getTSRext = boolean. If True, the extended TSR is returned as well.
kernel(), kernel_kinetic_only(), kernel_constrained_jac() Compute and return [evals, Revec, Levec, f] for the full, kinetic and constrained Jacobian types. They are called by update_kernel(). is_changed() Returns True if an attribute of the object has been set since the last kernel calculation.

docs.title: Module functions
docs.text:
The methods of CanteraCSP are built on module-level functions, which can also be used directly, e.g. on data computed elsewhere.

eigsys(jac) Returns [evals, Revec, Levec] of a Jacobian, sorted by decreasing eigenvalue modulus, with complex-conjugate pairs stored as real and imaginary parts. evec_pos_ampl(Revec, Levec, f) Changes the sign of the basis vectors so that all the amplitudes are non-negative. timescales(evals) Returns the timescales \(1/|\lambda_i|\). findM(n_elements, stateYT, evals, Revec, tau, f, rtol, atol) Returns the number of exhausted modes. findH(n_elements, stateYT, evals, Revec, dt, f, rtol, atol, Tail) Returns the Head index \(H\), given the Tail index \(M\) and the time horizon dt. setEwt(y, rtol, atol) Returns the error weights \(\mathrm{rtol}\,|y| + \mathrm{atol}\). findTSR(n_elements, rhs, evals, Revec, f, M) Returns [TSR, weights]. TSRindices(weights, evals) Returns the participation indices of the modes to the TSR. TSR_participation_indices(TSRidx, CSPidx, normtype) Returns the participation indices of the processes to the TSR, given the mode-to-TSR indices and the per-mode CSP indices (API or TPI). CSP_amplitude_participation_indices(B, Smat, rvec, normtype, norm_cut=None) Returns the API [N\(_v \times\) 2N\(_r\)]. CSP_timescale_participation_indices(nr, JacK, evals, A, B, normtype, norm_cut=None) Returns the TPI [N\(_v \times\) 2N\(_r\)], given the per-reaction Jacobians JacK (see jac_contribution()). CSP_importance_indices(A, B, M, Smat, rvec, normtype, norm_cut=None) Returns [Ifast, Islow]. CSPIndices(Proj, Smat, rvec, normtype, norm_cut=None) Returns the generic indices of the projections \(\mathbf{P}\,\mathcal{S}_k\, r^k\), normalized row by row. CSP_pointers(A, B) Returns the CSP pointers, pointers[m, j] \(= (\mathbf{a}_m \mathbf{b}^m)_{jj}\). classify_species(stateYT, rhs, pointers, M, trace) Returns the classification ('fast', 'slow', 'trace') of the variables. detectFrozenModes(M, stateYT, Revec, Levec, Smat, rvec, rtol, atol) Returns a boolean mask (one entry per variable index) marking the modes among the first M whose projected reaction rates \(\sum_k |\mathbf{a}_m \mathbf{b}^m \mathcal{S}_k r^k|\) are all below the error weights \(\mathrm{rtol}\,|y| + \mathrm{atol}\) (frozen modes). Used by the full CSP analysis example. add_transport(rhs, Levec, Smat, rvec, rhs_convYT, rhs_diffYT) Returns the extended source term, amplitudes, stoichiometric matrix and rates vector used by the extended TSR.

docs.title: class GScheme
docs.text:
This class is an ODE system integrator based on the G-Scheme [6]. The class takes as input an instance of the CanteraCSP class, with the problem type (constP or constRho) already set.

The G-Scheme partitions the modes into fast (Tail), active and slow (Head) subspaces. Only the active dynamics are integrated, with an explicit RK4 scheme, while the fast and slow subspaces are accounted for by the tail and head corrections. The CSP basis can be reused for several steps (reuse = True). The algorithm is described in the CSP solver and G-Scheme theory page.

import PyCSP.Functions as cspF
import PyCSP.GScheme as gsc
gas = cspF.CanteraCSP('gri30.yaml')
...
solver = gsc.GScheme(gas)

docs.title: Instance attributes
docs.text: jacobiantype Type (string). Set/get the Jacobian type. Available choices are: 'full'. Defaults to 'full'. csprtolT Type (float). Set/get the CSP relative tolerance for the exhausted modes (Tail) calculation. Defaults to 1.0e-2. cspatolT Type (float). Set/get the CSP absolute tolerance for the exhausted modes (Tail) calculation. Defaults to 1.0e-8. csprtolH Type (float). Set/get the CSP relative tolerance for the slow modes (Head) calculation. Defaults to 1.0e-4. cspatolH Type (float). Set/get the CSP absolute tolerance for the slow modes (Head) calculation. Defaults to 1.0e-10. factor Type (float). Set/get the timestep safety factor. Defaults to 0.2. T Type (int, read-only). Get the current number of exhausted modes (Tail index). H Type (int, read-only). Get the current number of exhausted plus active modes (Head index). The number of slow modes is \(N_v - N_{el} - H\). y Type (array of float, read-only). Get the current system state in the form \([\,Y_1, \dots, Y_{N_s}, T\,]\). t Type (float, read-only). Get the current system time. dt Type (float, read-only). Get the current system timestep size. reuse Type (boolean). Activate/deactivate the CSP basis reuse. Defaults to False. reuseThr Type (float). Set/get the threshold for the CSP basis reuse: the basis is recomputed when the norm of the relative change of the Jacobian diagonal exceeds reuseThr, or after 250 consecutive reuses. Defaults to 1.0e-1. iter Type (int, read-only). Get the number of steps taken. lam, A, B, f, tau Type (arrays, read-only). Get the eigenvalues, right and left basis vectors, amplitudes and timescales currently used by the integrator. Tc, Hc Type ([N\(_v\)] array of float, read-only). Get the current tail and head corrections. normJac, basisStatus, skipBasis, updateBasis Type (float, int). Diagnostic quantities of the basis-reuse algorithm: norm of the relative change of the Jacobian diagonal, 1 if the basis was updated in the last step (0 if reused), number of consecutive reuses, total number of basis updates.

docs.title: class CSPsimplify
docs.text:
This class generates simplified (skeletal) kinetic mechanisms based on CSP [3]. The class takes as input an instance of the CanteraCSP class and a dataset. The instance should be initialized with the detailed mechanism. The dataset must be a 2D array, each row containing species mass fractions (in the order of the detailed mechanism), temperature and pressure: dataset = [Y_1, Y_2, ..., Y_N, T, P].

The algorithm is described in the mechanism simplification theory page.

import PyCSP.Functions as csp
import PyCSP.Simplify as simp
dtl_mech = csp.CanteraCSP('gri30.yaml')
simplifier = simp.CSPsimplify(dtl_mech, dataset)

docs.title: Instance attributes
docs.text: csprtol Type (float). Set/get the CSP relative tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation. Defaults to 1.0e-2. cspatol Type (float). Set/get the CSP absolute tolerance for the exhausted modes calculation. Defaults to 1.0e-8. scaled Type (boolean). Set/get the scaled option for the importance indices. When active, indices are normalized with respect to their maximum value. Defaults to True. targetset Type (set of strings). Set/get the set of target species. Example: {'CH4', 'H2O', 'CO2'}. TSRtargetset Type (boolean). Set/get the TSRtargetset option for the target set. When active, the user-defined targetset, which may also be empty, is augmented with the local TSR-relevant species: each state will have its own set of targets, based on the TSR-API indices. Defaults to False. TSRtol Type (float). Set/get the TSR-API tolerance for including species in the TSR target set. A species is included if it is involved in a reaction belonging to the smallest subset of reactions whose cumulative participation to the TSR exceeds TSRtol\(\,\cdot 100\%\). The higher the value of TSRtol, the more species will be included. Defaults to 0.5. problemtype Type (string). Set/get the problem type, among 'constP' and 'constRho'. Defaults to 'constP'. norm_cut Type (float). Set/get the optional cut on the normalization of the importance and TSR indices (see calc_CSPindices in Functions.py). Only a scalar (or None) is accepted, because the same cut is applied to the importance indices (one row per variable) and to the TSR participation indices (one row per mode). Defaults to None. New in v1.5. verbose Type (boolean). Print progress information. Defaults to False. nv, ns, nr Type (int, read-only). Number of variables, species and reactions of the detailed mechanism.

docs.text:
dataset_info() Outputs info on dataset, including an estimate of the processing time. Note that this method changes the state of the gas object. process_dataset() Computes the fast/slow importance indices and the species fast/slow classification for each state in dataset. simplify_mechanism(threshold)

Returns the lists of retained species and reactions (Cantera Species and Reaction objects), based on the value of threshold, which must be between 0 and 1. A simplified mechanism is created as:

species, reactions = simplifier.simplify_mechanism(0.1)
skeletal = csp.CanteraCSP(thermo='ideal-gas', kinetics='gas', species=species, reactions=reactions)

docs.title: class CSPsolver
docs.text:
This class is an ODE system integrator based on the CSP method. The class takes as input an instance of the CanteraCSP class, with the problem type (constP or constRho) already set.

At each step the solver applies the radical correction for the \(M\) exhausted modes and integrates the projected system \(\dot{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{Q}_s\,\mathbf{g}\) with an explicit RK4 scheme. The algorithm is described in the CSP solver and G-Scheme theory page.

import PyCSP.Functions as cspF
import PyCSP.Solver as cspS
gas = cspF.CanteraCSP('hydrogen.yaml')
...
solver = cspS.CSPsolver(gas)

docs.title: class CanteraThermoKinetics
docs.text:
This class inherits attributes and methods from Cantera's Solution class and extends its capabilities by adding thermodynamics and kinetics-related class methods. Hence, the constructor for this class is equivalent to the constructor of Cantera's Solution class. The proper way to instantiate CanteraThermoKinetics objects is by using species and reactions defined in an input file, e.g. hydrogen.yaml:

import PyCSP.ThermoKinetics as csp
gas = csp.CanteraThermoKinetics('hydrogen.yaml')

Different formulations exist for the majority of this class methods depending on whether the reactor is considered having a constant pressure or a constant volume (density). Hence, it is mandatory to choose between constant pressure and constant density after instantiating an object of the CanteraThermoKinetics class and before accessing its attributes. The choice is made by defining either the pressure value or the density value through the attributes constP or constRho (see below). A lack of this choice will raise an exception when accessing the class attributes having multiple formulations.

The equations implemented by this class are described in the Theory page.

docs.title: Instance attributes
docs.text: constP Type (float). Set/get the thermodynamic pressure [Pa] and activates the constant pressure version of all the class methods (problemtype == 'const_p'). constRho Type (float). Set/get the thermodynamic density [kg/m\(^3\)] and activates the constant volume version of all the class methods (problemtype == 'const_v'). problemtype Type (string, read-only). Get the active definition of problemtype, either 'const_p' or 'const_v'. nv Type (int). Set/get the number of variables. Defaults to n_species + 1. The only alternative value is n_species, e.g., to exclude temperature from the list of variables and get appropriately sized objects from the class methods. It is set automatically by the jacobiantype attribute of CanteraCSP. source Type ([N\(_s\)+1] array of float, read-only). Get the chemical source term \([\,g_1, \dots, g_{N_s}, g_T\,]\) for the species mass fractions and temperature, based on either the constant pressure or constant volume formulation. jacobian Type ([N\(_s\)+1 \(\times\) N\(_s\)+1] array of float, read-only). Get the numerical Jacobian of the chemical source term, based on either the constant pressure or constant volume formulation. generalized_Stoich_matrix Type ([N\(_v\) \(\times\) 2N\(_r\)] array of float, read-only). Get the generalized stoichiometric matrix, based on either the constant pressure or constant volume formulation. Depending on the value of nv, the last row (temperature coefficients) is returned or not. R_vector Type ([2N\(_r\)] array of float, read-only). Get the rates of progress vector (forward rates followed by backward rates) [kmol/m\(^3\)/s]. jacobian_diagonal Type ([N\(_s\)+1] array of float, read-only). Get an inexpensive approximation of the Jacobian diagonal, obtained with a single simultaneous perturbation of all the variables. Used by the basis-reuse heuristic of the G-Scheme.

docs.title: Class methods
docs.text:
set_stateYT(state)

Set the thermochemical state of the mixture. This is an alternative to separately setting Cantera's attributes Y and either TP or TD. Pressure and density are automatically set based on the values of constP or constRho.

Mandatory positional arguments:

  • state (array of float). Array containing the mass fractions \(Y_i\) of all the species and the temperature: \([\,Y_1, Y_2, \dots, Y_{N_s}, T\,]\). The order of the \(Y_i\) values must comply with the species ordering set at the class instantiation. This can be retrieved with the method species(). The mass fractions are normalized by Cantera.
stateYT() Returns the thermochemical state of the mixture \([\,Y_1, Y_2, \dots, Y_{N_s}, T\,]\). rhs_const_p()

Returns the constant-pressure chemical source term of the mixture \([\,g_1, \dots, g_{N_s}, g_T\,]_P\):

\[ g_i = rac{W_i}{ ho} \sum_{k=1}^{2 N_r} u_{ik}\, r^k \qquad i=1,\dots,N_s, \qquad g_T = - rac{1}{c_p} \sum_{i=1}^{N_s} h_i\, g_i \]

where \(W_i\) is the molecular weight of species \(i\), \( ho\) is the mixture density, \( u_{ik}\) is the molar stoichiometric coefficient of species \(i\) in reaction \(k\), \(r^k\) is the molar rate of progress of reaction \(k\), \(c_p\) is the mixture constant-pressure specific heat and \(h_i\) is the specific (per unit mass) enthalpy of species \(i\).

rhs_const_v()

Returns the constant-volume chemical source term of the mixture \([\,g_1, \dots, g_{N_s}, g_T\,]_v\):

\[ g_i = rac{W_i}{ ho} \sum_{k=1}^{2 N_r} u_{ik}\, r^k \qquad i=1,\dots,N_s, \qquad g_T = - rac{1}{c_v} \sum_{i=1}^{N_s} h_i\, g_i + rac{R\, T}{c_v} \sum_{i=1}^{N_s} rac{g_i}{W_i} \] generalized_Stoich_matrix_const_p()

Returns the constant-pressure generalized stoichiometric matrix \(\mathcal{S}\), defined as:

\[ \mathcal{S}_{i,k} = rac{W_i}{ ho}\, u_{ik} \quad i=1,\dots,N_s, \qquad \mathcal{S}_{N_s+1,k} = - rac{1}{ ho\, c_p} \sum_{i=1}^{N_s} W_i\, u_{ik}\, h_i \qquad k =1,\dots,2N_r \] generalized_Stoich_matrix_const_v()

Returns the constant-volume generalized stoichiometric matrix \(\mathcal{S}\), defined as:

\[ \mathcal{S}_{i,k} = rac{W_i}{ ho}\, u_{ik} \quad i=1,\dots,N_s, \qquad \mathcal{S}_{N_s+1,k} = - rac{1}{ ho\, c_v} \sum_{i=1}^{N_s} W_i\, u_{ik}\, h_i + rac{R\, T}{ ho\, c_v} \sum_{i=1}^{N_s} u_{ik} \qquad k =1,\dots,2N_r \] Rates_vector() Returns the molar rates of progress \(r^k\) vector of the mixture (forward rates followed by backward rates). jacobian_const_p()

Returns the constant-pressure numerically-evaluated Jacobian of the chemical source term of the mixture:

\[ \mathbf{J} = egin{bmatrix} \left. rac{\partial g_1}{\partial Y_1} ight|_{P,T} & \dots & \left. rac{\partial g_{1}}{\partial Y_{N_s}} ight|_{P,T} & \left. rac{\partial g_1}{\partial T} ight|_{P,Y} \ \vdots & \ddots & & \vdots \ \left. rac{\partial g_{T}}{\partial Y_1} ight|_{P,T} & \dots & \dots & \left. rac{\partial g_T}{\partial T} ight|_{P,Y} \end{bmatrix} \]

Mass fractions are perturbed one at a time, without renormalization. See Theory for the finite-difference steps.

jacobian_const_v() Returns the constant-volume numerically-evaluated Jacobian of the chemical source term of the mixture, with derivatives taken at constant density instead of constant pressure. jac_contribution()

Returns a 2N\(_r\)-long array of [N\(_v\) \( imes\) N\(_v\)] Jacobian matrices, each one representing the contribution of reaction \(k\) to the Jacobian:

\[ \mathbf{J}_k = rac{\partial\, (\mathcal{S}_{k}\, r^k)}{\partial \mathbf{y}}, \qquad \sum_{k=1}^{2N_r} \mathbf{J}_k = \mathbf{J} . \]

The derivatives are taken with the same constraint (pressure or density) as jacobian. With nv = n_species, the species block is returned.

jacobian_diagonal_const_p(), jacobian_diagonal_const_v() Return the approximate Jacobian diagonal (see the attribute jacobian_diagonal) for the two formulations. jacKinetic() Returns the \(N_s imes N_s\) Jacobian, excluding the temperature row/column. jacThermal() Returns the \(N_s imes N_s\) correction \(\mathbf{J}_{YT}\,\mathbf{e}^T/c\) such that jacKinetic() - jacThermal() is the Jacobian constrained to constant enthalpy (constant pressure, \(e_j = h_j\), \(c = c_p\)) or constant internal energy (constant volume, \(e_j = u_j\), \(c = c_v\)). See Theory. jacSIM(Jac, major_ind, Levec)

Returns the Jacobian constrained to the SIM. Theoretical details can be found in [5].

Mandatory positional arguments:

  • Jac ([N\(_v imes\) N\(_v\)] array of float). A Jacobian matrix.
  • major_ind ([N\(_{major}\)] array of integers). A list of integers corresponding to the progressive index of the variables deemed as major.
  • Levec ([N\(_v imes\) N\(_v\)] array of float). A left eigenvectors matrix.
reaction_names() Returns the names of the chemical reactions (forward + backward), in the form '(Rf-k) equation' and '(Rb-k) equation'.

docs.text: integrate_batch_constP(gas, temperature, pressure, eqratio, FuComp, OxComp, tend, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-15) Integrates a constant-pressure batch reactor from the given initial temperature, pressure and equivalence ratio (fuel and oxidizer compositions as Cantera strings) up to tend.
